newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT-Israel Chemicals a buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Israel Chemicals a buy.

text.p: UBS Global Research has rated Israel Chemicals and its Dead Sea Works and Dead Sea Bromine subsidiaries as buys in a report issued on Tuesday.

Daniel Carasso, UBS's director of Israel research, estimated 1996 earnings for Israel Chemicals at $0.067 per share. He said this year's earnings per share (EPS) would reach $0.103 and $0.130 in 1998.
Carasso estimated Dead Sea Works' 1996 EPS at $0.14, rising to $0.18 this year and $0.21 in 1998. Dead Sea Bromine would post EPS of $0.36 1996, rising to $0.40 this year and $0.51 in 1998, he said.
Based on their share prices at the end of January, Israel Chemicals is trading at an 8.3 times 1998 earnings, Dead Sea at 13.2 and Bromine at 10.8.

"While these three companies trade at multiples similar to their international comparables, their 18-20 percent five-year growth rates are markedly higher than the 5-6 percent average five-year growth of their international peers," Carasso said.

Long-term EPS growth of more than 20 percent from its new magnesium project makes Dead Sea Works' stock "compelling", he said. "The major concerns are new project risk with magnesium, and always-present potential downside in potash prices," the report said.
Dead Sea Works, which gets most of its revenues today from potash, has a joint venture with Volkswagen AG to build a ferrous magnesium plant.

"Dead Sea Bromine offers 20 percent plus growth owing to the success of its flame retardants, reasonable cash flow generaton, a geared but still acceptable balance sheet and, very importantly, a low-risk strategy," the report said.
